news.title: Quantum effect could reverse gravity and violate Einstein’s theory of relativity
paras: A hallmark of gravity as we know it is that it pulls objects with mass together: gravity explains why the moon orbits Earth, and why an apple falls to the ground after detaching from the tree. While this is well established, there is still no agreement on how gravity works at scales dominated by quantum effects, and what quantum properties it may have.

Now, two research teams have independently found that quantum effects can make gravity act repulsively, pushing objects apart instead of pulling them together. “Anti-gravity or repulsion: no one has seen that before,” says Sougato Bose at University College London, who co-authored the other study with Lev Vaidman at Tel Aviv University in Israel.

news.title: There's an impostor hiding in the Hyades star cluster. Can you spot it?
paras: Aldebaran looks for all the world like the brightest member of the Hyades star cluster. It isn't — and discovering why changes the way you look at constellations.

There was the Hyades, the big V-shaped cluster that forms the bull's face, with Aldebaran, noticeably brighter and more orange than the other stars, the dominant star. Every diagram reinforced the arrangement — Aldebaran was the eye of Taurus, the Hyades made the face, and in my head they became one object. Then I discovered that Aldebaran has nothing to do with the Hyades.
